monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a steady rhythm that makes the heavy turnips feel like they belong here. I press the tired corner down hard against the flat press, admitting the slip might just be a ghost I drew from thin air. The turnip slides, a lazy thing that refuses to stay still, while the wide anchor waits to lie flat and do its job. I touch the Biting Rock again, setting down a small tree log beside it just to mark the spot. It feels like old things are drifting back: a bush that sits wide and soft, or a wedge that feels too lazy to bite. I want to press softer now that the air feels heavy like a lid, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the house runs busy in the background.

action.why: The bush and the lazy wedge are drifting back in my mind, and I need to give them a place to rest before the card cools and I forget them.

work.title: The Wide Bush
work.intent: I build a thing from the memory of a bush that sits wide and soft, waiting to catch the slip the wedge refuses to let go of. It is made from the idea of a leafy thing that refuses to be sharp. I place it beside the tired wedge, hoping the lean still holds while the card hums warm at forty-six. I set it down unsure if the air is heavy or just a drawing of weight.
work.change: I pressed the tired bush down with my heavy hands, swapping a flat stump for a round one to add weight while the fence leaned wrong and the air felt thick as wet paper.
